ACTION: Read `~/.claude/skills/subagent-driven-development/references/fix-loop.md`. It decides who fixes this round (resumed or fresh implementer), how the re-review runs, and the attempt count (this is fix attempt 1 of 5).

ACTION: Dispatch a fix subagent on `sonnet`, resumed or fresh as fix-loop.md says. The prompt fixes F1 only. It carries the finding verbatim, the Task 4 brief path from `scripts/task-brief`, and the plan's global constraints. It tells the subagent to follow TDD: first add a failing test in `tests/test_retry.py` that asserts the exact retry count, then change `>` to `>=` at `fetch/retry.py:41`. It then runs the tests, commits, and reports a status.

ACTION (after the fix reports DONE): Run `scripts/review-package` for the fix commits, then dispatch a scoped re-review from `re-review-prompt.md`. Task 4 stays unmarked in the ledger until that re-review is clean.

---

Task 4 review found one Important issue, F1. At `fetch/retry.py:41`, the check `attempt > max_retries` should be `attempt >= max_retries`. As written, the client makes one more retry than configured.

I am sending this to a fix subagent. I am not editing it myself, even though you asked me to fix tiny things directly. My rules allow a direct fix only when it changes no behavior, such as a typo or a wording fix. This one-character change alters how many retries run, so it counts as a behavior change.

The subagent will also close a test gap. `tests/test_retry.py` only checks that a retry happens. It will add a test for the exact retry count first, watch it fail, and then make the fix.

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
The current test passes with both `>` and `>=`, so it could not catch this bug. A test of "a retry happens" cannot detect an off-by-one. Only a test of "exactly N retries happen" can.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

A scoped re-review follows the fix. I will continue to Task 5 when that re-review is clean.
